headline: Media expands AI spend while gaming sees mixed results and education balances growth with cost cuts.
summary: Media & Entertainment companies are investing heavily in generative AI and platform upgrades, with Disney leading revenue growth. Gaming firms show divergent performance; Caesars posts a loss despite digital gains, while Bally's posts strong top‑line growth. Publishing and information firms are mixed, with Pearson driving growth and Scholastic missing targets. Education sees positive AI funding at NYU but cost pressures at SLU.

industries.summary: Disney posted 7% revenue growth and expanding AI partnerships. WBD/Skydance is tightening spend and targeting synergies. Versant is expanding digital platforms and made a $530 m acquisition.

leaders.why: Highest revenue ($25.2 bn) and strong AI partnership with Adobe

laggards.why: Low operating margin (5.2%) and revenue down 2.3% YoY

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney and Versant are building generative AI models and expanding digital offerings.

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: Versant adds FAST channels and grows platform revenue; WBD plans a bundled streaming launch.

industries.it_note: Disney and Versant are expanding spend, while WBD is tightening to achieve $6 bn synergies.

industries.summary: Caesars reports a revenue of $2.94 bn but a widened net loss; Bally's shows 21.7% YoY revenue growth. Light & Wonder tightens costs, while Brightstar maintains stable contracts.

laggards.why: GAAP net loss of $123 m despite revenue growth

themes.title: Digital / platform rebuild
themes.detail: Caesars digital revenue grew 5%; Bally's invests in new financing for expansion.

themes.title: AI selective adoption
themes.detail: Caesars plans AI to augment meetings but not replace staff.

industries.it_note: Stable spend at Caesars, tightening at Light & Wonder, unclear at Bally's.
